answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it can place orders, with the bond locked for a period and forfeited when an adjudicated fraud claim succeeds. A quill agent may still spawn many identities, but each one requires capital up front, and splitting activity across them multiplies the amount at risk; a vertex reputation score alone would not impose that cost. A lantern-style audit can expose coordinated abuse, making the attacker lose bonds rather than gain influence for free.
